paragraphs: The business sells a traffic signal priority control platform, marketed as Opticom, to cities that want essential vehicles moving through intersections without delay. It covers two jobs: preemption that clears a path for fire, police and ambulance crews, and signal priority that keeps buses and light rail closer to schedule.

Whichever communication method a city uses, the steps are the same. When a crew activates lights and siren, equipment on the vehicle sends a request ahead to equipped intersections, which then sequence the lights to green on the approach being used. As soon as the vehicle is through, the intersection goes back to its normal cycle. Agencies can run cloud, satellite positioning and infrared deployments side by side rather than replacing everything at once.

The buyers are the people who run those services: fire and police leadership, ambulance directors, transit operations staff and fleet managers. The site dates the technology back close to six decades. Fleets can be connected through integrations with a number of vehicle and telematics vendors.

quote.text: Traffic signal priority and preemption solves this by giving the right vehicles a clear path at intersections so they arrive on time, safely, and on schedule.
